claims.say: Never host everything in one place. One failure hits all.
claims.quote: If you host all of your instances in a single location that is affected by a failure, none of your instances would be available.

claims.say: On AWS, regions are separate geographic areas. Each region has multiple, isolated locations known as Availability Zones.
claims.quote: Regions are separate geographic areas. ... Each Region has multiple, isolated locations known as Availability Zones.

claims.say: An AWS Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with independent and redundant power infrastructure, networking, and connectivity.
claims.quote: An Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with independent and redundant power infrastructure, networking, and connectivity in an AWS Region.

claims.say: AWS Availability Zones in a region are up to 60 miles apart, so one fire or flood is designed not to hit them all; close enough for single-digit millisecond latency.
claims.quote: Availability Zones in a Region are meaningfully distant from each other, up to 60 miles (about 100 km) to prevent correlated failures, but close enough to use synchronous replication with single-digit millisecond latency. ... They’re designed to avoid simultaneous impact from shared fate scenarios such as utility power, water disruption, fiber isolation, earthquakes, fires, tornadoes, or floods.

claims.say: Say all instances run in Zone A; if Zone A fails, none would be available (example).
claims.quote: If you host all of your instances in a single location that is affected by a failure, none of your instances would be available.

claims.say: Spread across two Availability Zones, Zone A and Zone B; you can design your application so an instance in Zone B handles requests instead (example uses two zones).
claims.quote: If you distribute instances across multiple Availability Zones and an instance fails, you can design your application so that an instance in another Availability Zone handles requests instead.

claims.say: Azure's documentation says availability zones don't protect against a full-region outage.
claims.quote: Availability zones don't protect against a full-region outage.

claims.say: Spread it across zones; never keep everything in one place.
claims.quote: By launching EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones, you can protect your applications from the failure of a single location in the Region.
